column4: (2) The complaint given orally shall be reduced to writing

column3: in the language it was given, by any officer of the Commission
as directed by the Commission as soon as possible:

column4: Provided that, if it is not possible for the officer to record

column3: the complaint in the language in which it is given, the officer
shall request that the complaint be given in writing. If the
complainant is unable to give it in writing, the officer shall
record the complaint in one of the national languages after
recording  the  reasons  for  doing  so  and  shall  read  over  the
record to the complainant or interpret it in the language such
person understands.

column4: (3) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other

column3: written law, a public authority or a law enforcement authority,
where in the exercise of its functions is of the opinion that an
offence under the provisions of this Act may have occurred
or suspected to have committed, such public authority or the
law  enforcement  authority  shall  refer  the  matter  to  the
Commission for investigation.

column4: (1)  Any  person  who  has  made  a  complaint  under

column3: section 43 shall be provided with an update of the basic steps
taken in relation to an investigation conducted under section
42  in  a  manner  which  does  not  hinder  the  progress  of  the

column4: (2) The provisions of subsection (1) of section 5 of the

column3: Right to Information Act, No. 12 of 2016 shall apply for any
information provided, shared or communicated as provided
for in this Act.

column4: Any person who has made a complaint under section

column3: 43  shall  be  provided  with  a  detailed  justification  by  the
